steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Marriage patterns: the marriage rate in the UK has fallen to its lowest level since records began. First marriages have declined; the average age of first marriage has risen (30 for women, 32 for men). Reasons: secularisation (less religious pressure), changing attitudes (cohabitation is now socially acceptable), women's economic independence (no longer need to marry for financial security). | Key Fact: Divorce: the divorce rate increased dramatically after the 1969 Divorce Reform Act (made 'irretrievable breakdown' sufficient grounds). Currently about 42% of marriages end in divorce. Reasons: easier divorce laws, less stigma, women's financial independence, rising expectations of marriage (Giddens: confluent love - relationships only survive while both partners are satisfied). |

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why the divorce rate has increased in the UK since the 1960s. | Describe the demographic changes affecting UK families and assess their social implications. | Evaluate whether the decline of marriage is a problem for society.
